verse: “Come now, let us reason together,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow; though they are as red as crimson, they will become like wool.
story: God has just called heaven and earth as witnesses against His people, and the case looks lost; then the Judge Himself steps down and offers terms.

Judah had kept every feast and filled the courts with offerings, while their hands were stained with injustice toward the widow and the orphan. God refused the ritual and named the stain. Scarlet and crimson were dyes that soaked deep into cloth; no amount of scrubbing could lift them. Yet the LORD promises what no washer could do: snow, and wool still white from the flock. The cleansing is His work, and it calls for a willing, obedient heart in return. Isaiah will later show the cost of it in a Servant wounded for our transgressions.
Come to Him today without excuses or bargains. The stain you cannot lift, He can make white.
theme: Lent: repentance, the road to the cross
